mcqs.question: Which of the following statements about a unit cell is **incorrect**?

options.A: The unit cell is the smallest repeating unit that shows the entire symmetry of the crystal.
options.B: The unit cell always contains an integer number of atoms.
options.C: The unit cell edges are always equal in length.
options.D: The unit cell can be chosen such that its faces are parallel to the crystallographic axes.

mcqs.answer: The unit cell edges are always equal in length.
mcqs.explanation: Only cubic unit cells have equal edge lengths. In tetragonal, orthorhombic, monoclinic, etc., the edges differ. The other statements correctly describe properties of a unit cell. Hence option C is the misconception.

mcqs.learning_point: Identify primitive and centred unit cells
mcqs.question: A crystal lattice has lattice points located only at the eight corners of the cell and nowhere else. Which type of unit cell does this description correspond to?
mcqs.explanation: A primitive unit cell contains lattice points only at its corners. Body‑centred and face‑centred cells have additional points inside the cell (body centre or face centres). Therefore the correct identification is the primitive cubic cell.

mcqs.question: Among the crystal structures listed below, which one possesses the **lowest** coordination number?
mcqs.explanation: Coordination number (CN) is the number of nearest neighbours surrounding an atom. Simple cubic has the fewest neighbours (6), while BCC has 8 and both FCC and HCP have the highest possible for close‑packed structures (12). Hence option A is the lowest.

mcqs.question: Which lattice type generally yields the highest density for a given atomic radius?
mcqs.explanation: Density depends on packing efficiency. FCC (and HCP) have a packing efficiency of 74 %, the highest among the common Bravais lattices. Simple cubic packs only 52 % and BCC about 68 %. Therefore FCC gives the greatest density for the same atomic radius.

mcqs.question: A crystal lattice is best described as:

options.A: An arrangement of atoms in a regular repeating pattern extending in three dimensions.
options.B: The smallest repeating unit containing a single atom.
options.C: The external shape of a crystal specimen.
options.D: The set of all possible chemical bonds in a material.

mcqs.answer: An arrangement of atoms in a regular repeating pattern extending in three dimensions.
mcqs.explanation: A crystal lattice refers to the infinite, periodic array of points (or atoms) that repeats in three dimensions, defining the internal order of a crystalline solid. The other options describe different concepts.

mcqs.question: What is the definition of a unit cell in crystallography?

options.A: The smallest repeating unit of a crystal lattice that, when stacked together, recreates the entire lattice.
options.B: A single atom isolated from any lattice.
options.C: The macroscopic shape of a crystal specimen.
options.D: A hypothetical construct that has no physical significance.

mcqs.answer: The smallest repeating unit of a crystal lattice that, when stacked together, recreates the entire lattice.
mcqs.explanation: The unit cell is the fundamental building block of a crystal lattice; by translating it along the lattice vectors, the whole crystal can be generated. It is not merely a single atom nor a macroscopic shape.

mcqs.learning_point: Identify primitive and centred unit cells
mcqs.question: Which statement correctly distinguishes a primitive unit cell from a centred unit cell?

options.A: A primitive cell has lattice points only at its corners, whereas a centred cell has additional lattice points inside the faces or body of the cell.
options.B: A primitive cell contains extra lattice points inside the cell, while a centred cell has points only at the corners.
options.C: Both primitive and centred cells have the same number of lattice points; the difference is only in shape.
options.D: Centred cells are used only for molecular crystals, whereas primitive cells are for ionic crystals.

mcqs.answer: A primitive cell has lattice points only at its corners, whereas a centred cell has additional lattice points inside the faces or body of the cell.
mcqs.explanation: In a primitive unit cell, the only lattice points are at the eight corners (each contributing 1/8 to the cell). Centred cells (body‑centred, face‑centred, etc.) have extra points at the centre of the body or on the faces, increasing the number of lattice points per cell.

mcqs.question: In a crystal where each ion is surrounded by six nearest‑neighbour ions, the coordination number of the ion is:
mcqs.explanation: Coordination number is the count of nearest neighbours surrounding a central atom or ion. If an ion has six nearest neighbours, its coordination number is 6. The other numbers correspond to different lattice types.
